Our Mutual Friend. Serialized from 1864 to 1865, this is Charles Dickens's final completed novel. It is set in Victorian London in a world obsessed with money, dust, and moral corruption. The narrative weaves together multiple interlocking plots centered on John Harmon, a man who was presumed drowned but mysteriously returns in disguise to observe the world. Part of what he wants to watch is Bella Wilfer, a young woman who was intended to marry him according to a will. Bella begins as a materialistic young woman who values fortune and appearances above all else. But through the course of the novel, she undergoes a profound transformation, discovering that true wealth lies not in money or status but in the heart. At the center of her change is the realization of genuine love. Another central figure is Lizzie Hexam, a riverside girl who loves Eugene Wrayburn, a lawyer of good birth but morally dissolute character. Their relationship follows an arc of redemption through love. But this love is threatened by Bradley Headstone, a schoolmaster and rival for Lizzie's affection. Headstone embodies something dark and dangerous: the violent passions that lie hidden beneath a respectable exterior. His jealousy darkens the narrative significantly. Noddy Boffin, an honest dustman, unexpectedly inherits a fortune built from garbage. As he gains wealth, he becomes corrupted by money itself, before undergoing a redemptive reversal. The Thames River and the world of dust—refuse pickers and garbage—provide running metaphors for London's moral and economic underbelly, showing how money and corruption flow through every level of society.
